name: fetch_parslow_redirect
verification_note: genuine 2-step GOAP plan composed and executed against the REAL external host parslow.net (not a mock/local server); visible checks confirmed a real HTTP/1.1 301 response; a blind held-back check (the EXACT Location header value, not inspected until after the visible checks already passed) also matched, confirming the result isn't a vacuous 'some redirect happened' pass. CONFIRMED, HONEST LIMITATION: parslow.net is HTTPS-only and PatLang has no TLS support, so this genuinely cannot retrieve real page content (e.g. the actual bdd-retrofitting.html the user views over HTTPS in a browser) -- only the plain-HTTP redirect response, which is what this spec actually claims and verifies, nothing more.
known_gap_surfaced: PatLang's networking stack has no TLS/HTTPS client capability -- a real, separate, un-built feature, not a bug in this experiment
